title: OpenTelemetry vs Jaeger: Which One Actually Scales? ⚡
fb_caption:
OpenTelemetry vs Jaeger: Which Architecture Actually Scales in Production? ⚡

🚀 Throughput: OpenTelemetry's vendor-neutral approach offers broader integration and potentially higher throughput with dedicated backends.
⚡ Latency: Jaeger can offer lower latency for trace collection in self-hosted setups, but OpenTelemetry's sampling can manage overhead.
⚖️ Consistency: OpenTelemetry standardizes instrumentation, leading to more consistent data across diverse services. Jaeger is more focused on its own ecosystem.
💥 Failure Modes: OpenTelemetry's decoupled components can improve resilience. Jaeger's monolithic nature might present single points of failure if not managed.
🔧 Operational Overhead: OpenTelemetry can have higher initial setup complexity but offers flexibility. Jaeger is simpler for basic tracing but less adaptable.

Recommendation: For production environments prioritizing flexibility, broad compatibility, and future-proofing, OpenTelemetry is generally the stronger choice. Jaeger remains excellent for focused, self-contained tracing needs.
